text.title: API Versioning Failure Modes
text.summary: 8 antipatterns observed in real deployments. Each pairs symptom + root cause + concrete fix.

antipattern.symptom: A required field is added to an existing v1 endpoint; existing clients fail validation the moment it deploys; outage.
antipattern.root-cause: Team read "new field" as always additive and missed that making it required tightens the contract.
antipattern.fix: Run the oasdiff classifier in CI and force a major bump on any field-required addition. See rules breaking-change-classifier + additive-first.

antipattern.symptom: Some endpoints carry the version in the path, others in the Accept header; the partner SDK has to support both.
antipattern.root-cause: Versioning scheme chosen ad-hoc per endpoint instead of once per API.
antipattern.fix: Pick one scheme, record it in info.x-versioning, enforce it with a Spectral rule. See rule one-scheme-per-api and templates/spectral-rules.yaml.

antipattern.symptom: v1 is deprecated "soon"; six months later it is still in use and nobody dares remove it.
antipattern.root-cause: No ISO date was ever published — the commitment lived in a blog post and a verbal promise.
antipattern.fix: Publish a Sunset header with a concrete ISO date at least 90 days out for public APIs. See rule deprecation-window-declared.

antipattern.symptom: Client sends version: "v2" inside the request body; the CDN cannot cache and the proxy cannot route.
antipattern.root-cause: Author thought a body-level flag was "more flexible" than a path segment.
antipattern.fix: Move the version to the URL path or the Accept header and deprecate the body flag. See rule no-version-in-payload.

antipattern.symptom: Single handler dispatches between v1 and v2 response shapes via if/else inside business logic.
antipattern.root-cause: Author treated v1/v2 as 'duplication to remove'.
antipattern.fix: Move v1 to a frozen read-only module; v2 is a separate module/router. Forbid shared handlers in code review.

antipattern.symptom: 2-person team adopts Stripe-style date-based versioning with per-customer pinning.
antipattern.root-cause: Agents read the Stripe blog and copy the pattern without weighing operational cost.
antipattern.fix: Use URL path versioning at small scale; date-based requires a transformation pipeline that small teams cannot maintain.

antipattern.symptom: Agent decides 'v1 is deprecated' and deletes the handler in the same PR as the 410 Gone flip.
antipattern.root-cause: Sunset workflow not encoded as two PRs.
antipattern.fix: Block any PR that deletes a v1 handler unless preceded by 30 days of zero traffic AND a prior 410 Gone PR.

antipattern.symptom: Deprecation is announced in a blog post but the route still returns 200 with no Sunset/Deprecation headers.
antipattern.fix: Add a global middleware that injects Deprecation/Sunset/Link headers for any route marked deprecated in ops/sunset.yaml.
